transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-03-08
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Jared Rowe (CTO, Lakemont), Priya Singh (Head of Security), Anika Bose (Platform Engineer)

Topics: SOC2/ISO requirements, SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC model, audit logs & retention, encryption/KMS/HSM, hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment, network boundaries, compliance artifacts.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time, quick intros?
[00:12] Jared Rowe: yeah Jared here CTO, we'll be short. Priya is our security lead, Anika is on platform.
[00:20] Priya Singh: hi all - we want to validate controls quickly and understand deployment surface area.
[00:28] Maya Chen: perfect. high level, Redwood supports hosted API, reserved dedicated pools, and a private deployment (VPC/on-prem). Today we want to map your compliance constraints to those options.
[00:40] Owen Patel: hi, I'll cover technical bits - network, KMS integration, audit logging, RBAC. Quick Q - are you evaluating SOC2 and ISO together or separately?
[00:52] Priya Singh: both. SOC2 Type II is required for our vendor baseline. ISO 27001 is a nice-to-have for execs and some EU contracts. we need evidence for both.
[01:05] Maya Chen: got it. our security pack includes SOC2 report, ISO summary, plus a controls matrix mapping to our features. i'll send that after the call.
[01:15] Jared Rowe: do you have an NDA and any data processing agreement? that's also a gating item for legal.
[01:22] Maya Chen: yes, we have DPA templates and an NDA — i'll share links.
[01:27] Priya Singh: great. on host choices, what are the main differences from a controls perspective? especially around key management and data plane separation.
[01:40] Owen Patel: short answer: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value but keys are managed by Redwood by default; you can use customer-managed keys in some hosted tiers but the private control plane option gives you full KMS integration with your cloud KMS or on-prem HSM. dedicated is a middle ground — reserved capacity with stronger tenant isolation and optional BYOK.
[02:02] Anika Bose: when you say BYOK optional, that means the kv cache and tokenization keys are in our KMS? curious about how much data ever touches Redwood-managed secrets.
[02:14] Owen Patel: right. with BYOK we provision encryption keys in your KMS and Redwood stores only wrapped keys. runtime secrets and ephemeral keys are rotated; persistent artifacts like audit logs can be pushed to your log storage. small caveat: for hosted public Tier some telemetry metadata is retained for observability — we can control retention windows.
[02:36] Priya Singh: telemetry metadata — can you clarify? we need to know if PII or customer data is ever present.
[02:44] Maya Chen: in general we minimize PII in telemetry. prompts and outputs are treated as customer data; retention depends on plan and settings — for Private you control retention; for Hosted there are configurable retention windows and a policy for deletion on request. we'll share the retention policy doc.
[03:05] Jared Rowe: our EU customers require data residency and audit trails for 7 years, so we're leaning to Private in a VPC to control logs and retention.
[03:16] Owen Patel: private deployment supports hosting in your region and exporting logs to your SIEM/ELK with configurable retention, including long-term cold storage. audit logs include token-level request IDs, timestamp, model variant, route, and auth principal.
[03:35] Priya Singh: what about SSO? we use Okta and SAML 2.0, SCIM for provisioning. we need role sync and least-privilege access.
[03:46] Owen Patel: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM. RBAC is configurable with role templates, and you can map your Okta groups to Redwood roles. for Private, you can host the identity provider connector inside your VPC.
[04:00] Anika Bose: does SCIM push include disabled users, deprovision events?
[04:04] Owen Patel: yes it supports full lifecycle: create, update, deactivate. some timing caveats around eventual consistency, but we've shipped production SCIM integrations with several customers.
[04:16] Priya Singh: auditability of admin operations is critical — can we see who changed roles, who rotated keys, who created model pins?
[04:25] Owen Patel: admin audit trails are available across all deployment modes; on Hosted we retain them per plan settings and can export; on Private you own the logs. they include actor, action, resource, timestamp, and pre/post state where feasible.
[04:42] Jared Rowe: encryption at rest and in transit — we use TLS internally, but we need HSM-backed key material for certain customers. do you support HSMs?
[04:52] Owen Patel: yes — on Private we integrate with customer HSMs via KMIP or cloud KMS with customer-managed keys; we support HSM attestation workflows for higher assurance. Hosted supports cloud-KMS BYOK in supported clouds.
[05:05] Maya Chen: just to call out, for regulatory audits we can provide key rotation logs, KMS access logs, and attestations — we'll include an artifacts list.
[05:15] Priya Singh: sounds good. next — retention and deletion. we need legal holds and export capability for e-discovery.
[05:25] Owen Patel: we support retention policies at workspace and route levels; legal hold overrides deletion and you can export raw logs & transcripts via API. for long-term retention we can integrate with S3 Glacier or your archival solution.
[05:39] Anika Bose: any constraints on model caching or KV cache — could it leak across tenants in Dedicated?
[05:45] Owen Patel: no cross-tenant leakage — KV caches are tenant-scoped. in Dedicated there's hardware isolation plus process-level separation; Private gives you network-level isolation as well. small misrecognition: sometimes the transcript says K V cash — but it's KV cache.
[06:00] Jared Rowe: do you have a CIP or penetration test reports? we need to see third-party pentest summary.
[06:08] Maya Chen: yes, we have recent pen test reports and vulnerability management summary — i'll add those links.
[06:15] Priya Singh: incident response — what's your typical SLA and notification process?
[06:21] Owen Patel: we have an on-call SRE and an incident response runbook; for Enterprise/Dedicated we provide phone/email incident notifications and post-incident reports. SLA for incident acknowledgement depends on support tier.
[06:37] Anika Bose: network topology — if we go Private inside our VPC, does Redwood require peering, or can we run fully air-gapped?
[06:46] Owen Patel: Private supports both models — we have an air-gapped on-prem package for sensitive environments; for cloud VPC we typically use VPC peering or private endpoints; control plane can be customer-managed in some engagements.
[07:00] Maya Chen: just want to surface typical timeline — private deployment pre-flight is ~6-8 weeks for initial validation, depending on infra readiness; dedicated can be faster if you accept some managed elements.
[07:12] Jared Rowe: budgets — we care about latency too; low latency for EU customers is important, will need local region support. do you have benchmarks for token p99?
[07:22] Owen Patel: we publish model latency profiles for common instance types; p95/p99 depends on model and batch settings; we can run a short benchmark under PoC to validate.
[07:34] Priya Singh: okay. one more question — do Redwood engineers have access to production data for debugging?
[07:42] Maya Chen: access is role-based and audited. in Hosted some support access is allowed under strict controls and only with customer approval; with Dedicated/Private you can opt to restrict or require jumpbox access and session recording. all access is logged.
[07:58] Anika Bose: what's the default log retention on Hosted? we need to know how long transcripts are kept if we forget to change settings.
[08:06] Owen Patel: default is 30 days for detailed transcripts and 90 days for aggregated metrics on the basic hosted plan; enterprise plans increase retention; you can request longer through contract addenda.
[08:20] Priya Singh: can we run a short spike — private control plane in our EU region with key rotation policies and log export to our SIEM?
[08:29] Maya Chen: yes that's the typical pilot — we'll propose a scoping doc.
[08:33] Jared Rowe: ok next steps from our side: Anika will gather retention rules and regulatory constraints.
[08:40] Priya Singh: and legal will need DPA and SOC2.
[08:45] Maya Chen: action items noted — i'll circulate artifacts and schedule follow-up.

[08:55] End of meeting recap by Maya: recap: MVP pilot = Private control plane in EU, BYOK via customer KMS, audit log export, SAML/SCIM integration, 7-year retention path. deliverables: security pack, deployment pre-flight checklist, high level network diagram & cost/latency benchmarks.

References/links shared during call:
- Redwood security pack (SOC2, ISO summary): https://redwood.ai/security-pack (shared post-call)
- Private deployment pre-flight checklist (doc): https://redwood.ai/private-checklist
- Example network diagram (will attach): note: diagram link to be provided by Owen

Audio artifacts note: auto-transcription contains occasional mis-words: "K V cash" for KV cache, "S A M L" spelled out in pieces, and some punctuation omissions.
